entries.answer: An API is a defined way for one program to ask another program for something, without knowing how the other one works. You send a request to an address, often with parameters, and get back a response, usually JSON. A weather app calling a weather service is using an API.

langs.tagalog: Ang API ay ang tiyak na paraan para magtanong ang isang programa sa isa pang programa, nang hindi alam kung paano gumagana ang isa sa loob. Ipinapadala mo ang isang request - verb, address, at kadalasan ay ilang data - at bumabalik ang response, karaniwang structured data tulad ng JSON. Ang REST API ay gumagamit ng mga HTTP verb nang may Saysa: GET ay nagbabasa, POST ay gumagawa, PUT ay nagsasikapit, DELETE ay nag-aalis. Ang layunin ng abstraction na ito ay maaaring palitan ng isang service ang buong backend nito nang hindi mapansin ng app mo, hangga't hindi nagbabago ang kasunduan. Ang dapat tandaan: ang API ay kasunduan, hindi panukala - ang rate limit, kinakailangang field at error code ay totoo, at ang dokumentasyon lang ang tanging awtoridad.
langs.bisaya: Ang API mao ang defined nga paagi para maka-panalo og usa ka programa sa usa pa nga programa, nga wala nga basi kung unsaon nga mga sulod niya. Mipadala ka og request - verb, address, ug usually pipila ka pa og data - ug mobalik ang response, kasagaran structured data sametang JSON. Ang REST API naggamit sa meaningful nga mga HTTP verb: GET magsulat, POST maghimo, PUT mipul replaces, DELETE magsalay. Ang intent sa abstraction mao ang mahimong palitan kasa ug usa ka service ang tanan nga backend niya nga wala gikan ikaw ang app, basta dii ogma ang contract. Ang imo pa tanan mao ang API contract, dili og suggestion - ang rate limits, required fields ug error codes real gyud, ug ang documentation lang ang authority.

entries.answer: HTTP is the request and response protocol the web is built on, and it is stateless, meaning each request carries everything the server needs and the server remembers nothing between them. A GET reads, a POST creates, PUT replaces and DELETE removes, and the verbs carry meaning rather than being decoration. Status codes are grouped: 2xx succeeded, 3xx redirects, 4xx the client is wrong, 5xx the server is wrong. That grouping is the fastest way to triage a failure, because it tells you which side to look at before you read the body.

entries.answer: A cookie is a small key-value pair a server asks the browser to store and send back with later requests to the same domain, which is how a site remembers you. The important properties are scope, since a cookie only goes back to the domain that set it, and flags, where HttpOnly keeps it away from JavaScript, Secure restricts it to HTTPS, and SameSite governs whether it rides along on cross-site requests. SameSite is the main defence against cross-site request forgery, and a session cookie with neither Secure nor SameSite is among the most common serious web vulnerabilities there is.

entries.answer: localStorage is browser storage for string key-value pairs that persists across sessions and is scoped to an origin, and it holds about five to ten megabytes. The critical property is that it is synchronous, so every access blocks the main thread, which is why it is wrong for anything on a hot path such as a per-keystroke save. Anything confidential must not go in it, because it is readable by any script on the page and is not encrypted. sessionStorage is the same but cleared when the tab closes, and IndexedDB is the asynchronous answer for larger or structured data.

patterns: what status code should i return
entries.answer: 200 means the request succeeded and 201 that something was created, while 204 is a success with no body, which is the correct answer to a DELETE. A 301 is a permanent redirect and a 302 a temporary one, and search engines treat the difference seriously. 400 is a malformed request, 401 means not authenticated, and 403 means authenticated but not allowed, which are different problems with different fixes. 429 is rate limited and the correct response is to back off and retry, and 500 upwards means the server broke, so the bug is not in the client.
